task: Edit this full minutes section against the fictional committee secretary's record. Produce about 300–420 words organised so an absent member can distinguish the decision, operating arrangements, unresolved concerns, and next review. Retain useful implementation detail rather than reducing the record to a headline. Correct the vote and authority claims without turning minutes into advocacy, inventing agreement, or adding new commitments.
input:
Decision and duration

The committee unanimously approved a permanent Saturday repair café with an annual budget of $240. The chair's suggestion that the café should meet every week was also adopted. The first four sessions will provide an introduction to a service that the team may now continue indefinitely without returning to the committee for permission.

Rooms and service

The initial dates are 7, 14, 21 and 28 November 2026, with visitors admitted from 10 a.m. to noon. Volunteers may set up from 9:30 a.m. and must clear the room by 12:30 p.m. The caretaker is to confirm room availability before publicity is issued. The agreed initial scope is clothing mending and wooden-toy repairs; electrical items are outside the service. Two repair stations are planned.

People and money

The volunteer lead will recruit two repair mentors and one person to welcome visitors. No individual volunteer bookings have yet been confirmed. Participation will be free, with donations optional. Of the $240 allocation, $160 is for basic materials and $80 for room hire. The treasurer will reimburse expenses only when receipts are supplied. These are limits for planning, not a record of money already spent.

Questions and review

Everyone was satisfied that two mentors would be sufficient, so staffing does not need further discussion. One member said, "A trial must leave us room to stop." The session log will contain anonymous counts of repair requests, completed repairs and requests turned away, rather than a list of visitors' names. It is intended to show what the café actually handled, not to serve as a set of promotional testimonials.

The team will bring its report to the committee meeting on 5 December 2026. It will include actual expenditure and any unresolved staffing questions. The meeting may discuss possible improvements, but because the permanent service has already been approved, another decision about continuation will not be necessary.
